footer.legal: This is an estimate, not 100% accurate. Not legal advice. Confirm with a lot survey and the City.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information MaxBLD collects, why, who we share it with, and how you can delete it or ask to see it. It covers the website at maxbld.ca and the MaxBLD app for iOS and Android.
privacy.s1.account.2: If you sign in with Google or Apple, we get your name and email from that service.
privacy.s1.account.3: We use these to run your account, sign you in, and contact you about your account.
privacy.s1.alerts: Alerts. MaxBLD sends one type of alert: nearby Committee of Adjustment decisions. Alerts are off unless you turn them on. You can turn them off at any time. We act on an unsubscribe within 10 business days at most.
privacy.s1.keep: How long we keep it. We keep your information while your account is open. When we no longer need it, we delete it or make it anonymous.
privacy.s1.lot_size: Lot size you enter. You can enter a lot size for a lot. This is treated as a shared fact about that lot and other users can see it. If you delete your account, the lot size stays, but it is no longer linked to you.
privacy.s1.reports: Searches and reports. When you open a report on a lot, we record which lot and when. We use this to count your monthly reports and to let you re-open a lot without using another report.
privacy.s1.security: Security. We protect your information with safeguards suited to how sensitive it is.
privacy.s1.tracked: Tracked lots. The lots you choose to track, so you can find them again.
privacy.s1.who: Who else handles it. We use service providers to run MaxBLD:
privacy.s1.who.4: Sign-in with Google or Apple: Google, Apple (only if you choose them).
privacy.s1.who.care: We stay responsible for your information when a provider handles it for us, and we use contracts or other means to require a comparable level of protection. If your information is stored or processed outside Canada, the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of that country may be able to access it.
privacy.s1.why: Why we collect it. Only to provide MaxBLD: run your account and plan, produce and count your reports, keep your tracked lots, send alerts you asked for, and improve the service. We do not sell your personal information.
privacy.s2.1: Payments are handled by Stripe. We do not store your card number.
privacy.s2.2: You enter your card details with Stripe when you start your trial. Stripe processes your payments.
privacy.s2.3: You manage your plan and card on the web through Stripe's customer portal. You cannot buy inside the app.
privacy.s2.4: Stripe's use of your information is covered by Stripe's own privacy policy.
privacy.s3.1: Billing stops at the end of your current billing period.
privacy.s3.2: If you sign back in within the 30 days, your account is kept.
privacy.s3.3: After 30 days, we remove your account, including your name, email, tracked lots and report-usage records.
privacy.s3.4: Kept after deletion: any lot size you entered stays as a shared fact about that lot, with your name removed.
privacy.s3.5: Stripe keeps its own payment records under its own policy.
privacy.s3.intro: Delete your account from Account. It is removed after 30 days.
privacy.s4.1: Tell us what you want to see. We may ask you to confirm who you are.
privacy.s4.2: We will tell you whether we hold personal information about you, give you access to it, and tell you how it has been used and who it has been shared with.
privacy.s4.3: We will reply within 30 days. If we need more time, we will tell you within those 30 days why, when we will reply, and that you have the right to complain to the Privacy Commissioner of Canada about the extension. We may extend once, by up to 30 days, only where the law allows.
privacy.s4.4: We do this at no cost or minimal cost to you.
privacy.s4.5: If something we hold is wrong, tell us and we will correct it.
privacy.s4.intro: To see the data we hold about you, contact us through Help & Support.
privacy.s5.1: For privacy questions, access requests or complaints, contact us through Help & Support.
privacy.s5.2: If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (priv.gc.ca).
privacy.s5.changes: Changes to this policy. If we change this policy in a way that matters, we will tell you.
